review_evidence: README describes kernel-checkable primality proofs using Pocklington and a cube-root variant, with generated certificates only as an auxiliary convenience.
Fifteen of 30 Lean files contain proposition declarations, including Pocklington correctness, modular exponentiation lemmas and explicit primality/certificate examples.
The metaprogramming is backed by substantive theorem-level primality verification, so source retirement or hard exclusion would lose formal prior art.
summary: Reviewed PrimeCert; retain the verified Pocklington primality machinery and certificate theorems.

summary: Surveyed all 15 listed files under the checkout root, MillerRabin/, PrimeCert/ and PrimeCert/Meta/ with sizes and a word-boundary declaration grep (theorem|lemma|def|structure|instance|abbrev|elab|macro|syntax|simproc|inductive). Every non-aggregator file carries Lean declarations: kernel-reducible Pocklington certificates, PowMod, a kernel-checked sieve of Eratosthenes with its correctness proofs, bounded Bool quantifiers, Miller-Rabin definitions, and the tactics that build these proofs. MillerRabin.lean and PrimeCert.lean are import-only aggregators; under FILTER-007 and FD-016 they stay primary-eligible and are ranked as navigation, not filtered. Disposition: retain all; no exclusions.
